title: Draw anywhere in the reader, including the margins
acceptance: With the markup tool active, a stroke can be drawn anywhere over the page - across blocks, in the left and right margins, and in the space between blocks
Drawing works in full screen; entering markup does not require leaving immersive reading
Ink still anchors to the document, not the screen: a mark drawn at one text size sits in the same place at another, and survives a re-render
Existing strokes drawn under the old per-block canvas render unchanged, with no migration
While the markup tool is inactive, scrolling and text selection behave exactly as they do today
notes: User request: mark up anywhere in full screen, and write in the margins. WHY IT CANNOT WORK TODAY: InkCanvas mounts inside ArticleBlockView, which sits inside ReaderView's .frame(maxWidth: typography.measure) column. The margins are the padding OUTSIDE that column, so a per-block canvas can never reach them. The fix is a document-level ink layer in ReaderView spanning the full width. THE ANCHORING MODEL IS ALREADY RIGHT AND MUST NOT BE REPLACED: InkStroke stores blockIndex plus points in that block's unit space, which is why a stroke drawn at 19pt New York still sits over the same sentence at 26pt SF Rounded. Its own doc comment already anticipates out-of-range values - a stroke running past the bottom of its block keeps a y above 1. Margins are the same idea on the x axis: anchor to the nearest block and let x fall below 0 or above 1. That keeps every existing stroke valid with no migration, which is criterion 4. Do not invent a second coordinate system.
